chunks: God does not burden a soul beyond capacity. Each will enjoy what (good) he earns, as indeed each will suffer from (the wrong) he does.
Punish us not, O Lord, if we fail to remember or lapse into error.
Burden us not, O Lord, with a burden as You did those before us.
Impose not upon us a burden, O Lord, we cannot carry.
Overlook our trespasses and forgive us, and have mercy upon us;
You are our Lord and Master, help us against the clan of unbelievers.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the supplication 'Rabbana la tu'akhidhna' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this verse is revered as the 'Verse of Burden' (Ayat al-Harb) and is frequently cited to support the concept of divine mercy and the exemption from strict accountability for unintentional errors (khata'). It serves as a foundational text for understanding the balance between human responsibility and God's grace, often recited in both daily prayers and supplications for relief from worldly trials.
